title: Detection of [O III]<SUB>88 μm</SUB> in JADES-GS-z14-0 at z = 14.1793
question: Can ALMA detect the [OIII] 88 um line in the z>10 galaxy GS-z14 to pin down its redshift, and what does it imply for its ISM (metallicity, density) and dust content

recipe.method: Standard ALMA pipeline calibration in CASA, 30 s time averaging, natural-weighted tclean with automasking to 2 sigma
Collapse moment maps over 75-350 km/s widths at every channel, list >3 sigma peaks, prune duplicates, repeat on the negative moment map
key_parameters: Duplicates pruned within 2xFWHM and 1.5x the beamsize

recipe.goal: Identify the line candidate and derive the redshift
recipe.method: Take the most significant candidate within 0.5 arcsec of the JWST position; convert its frequency to a [OIII]88 redshift

recipe.goal: Measure line FWHM and integrated flux
recipe.method: Iterative moment-zero map including channels within 2xFWHM; 1D spectrum from pixels >3 sigma; Gaussian fit for new FWHM
key_parameters: 1D spectrum extracted from all pixels with S/N > 3 sigma on the moment-zero map

recipe.goal: Derive [OIII]88 luminosity and compare with the local L-SFR relation
recipe.method: Convert the integrated flux to a lensing-corrected luminosity and compare with the local relation for metal-poor dwarfs
Dispersion-dominated estimate from the measured FWHM and r_[OIII] = r_e
assumptions: Dispersion-dominated; [OIII] radius equals the rest-UV effective radius

recipe.goal: Upper limits on dust continuum, dust mass and IR luminosity
recipe.method: Optically thin modified black body at fixed T_d and beta_IR with the Weingartner and Draine dust model, applied to the 3 sigma 90 um continuum limit
key_parameters: kappa_88 = 34.15 cm^-2 g^-1; L_IR integrated over 8-1000 um
assumptions: Dust temperature 60 K, justified by theory and observational trends extrapolated to z~14 and the CMB temperature

recipe.goal: Constrain ISM conditions from [OIII]88 versus MIRI [OIII]+Hbeta
recipe.method: Monte Carlo draws of [OIII]/Hbeta from the MIRI SED-fitting distribution to compute [OIII]5007 luminosity and compare to ALMA [OIII]88 on a Cloudy grid
key_parameters: Cloudy grids at fixed log U = -3.0 and -2.0, bracketing log U = -2.5 +/- 0.5
assumptions: Flat underlying continuum for the F770W excess of 27.5 +/- 5.6 nJy

recipe.method: Apply an empirical [OIII]88 + SFR oxygen-abundance calibration and compare with a Cloudy grid of [OIII]88/SFR versus ionisation parameter (1 Myr stellar population)
key_parameters: Cloudy grid with a 1 Myr old input stellar population
assumptions: Higher densities or older stellar ages would give higher metallicity (up to solar)

recipe.goal: Convert dust-to-stellar mass limit into a supernova dust yield limit and compare with the AFM
recipe.method: Dust yield per supernova from the dust-to-stellar mass limit (Salpeter IMF); compare predicted AFM continuum flux with the ALMA limit
assumptions: Salpeter IMF for the yield conversion

score_reason: Observing set-up, calibrator names, CASA version and imaging basics are given, but line-search thresholds, continuum construction and the Cloudy grid are not fully specified
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project code is printed and the archive links it to the paper; a single compact line detection and numeric flux, FWHM and continuum limits can be re-derived, though dust and ISM steps depend on external inputs
